items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is Qxf3.
A white bishop stands on f3.
The black queen stands on d3.
One white piece attacks f3: the pawn on g2.
Trading queens with Qxa6 is at least 30 centipawns below the top move.

hints: Look at the white bishop on f3 and ask which white pieces defend it.
Only one white piece defends it. Ask what a recapture there would do to the files near the white king.
The queen takes the bishop; after the pawn recaptures, a rook has a check on the g-file.
items.explain: In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine puts 17...Qxf3 first, ahead of the queen trade 17...Qxa6. Counting values are a rule of thumb: a queen for a bishop is a large deficit on paper. This is evidence for the game move at one depth, not proof.

feedback_by_move.d3a6: Trading queens is rated lower: at depth 16 the engine puts Qxa6 at least 30 centipawns below 17...Qxf3.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is Bh3.
The black bishop stands on d7.
Retreating with Bc8 is at least 150 centipawns below the top move.

hints: Which white pieces cover the squares near the white king, and can you attack one of them?
The bishop can go to a square where it attacks a white rook.
The bishop goes to h3, attacking the rook on f1.
items.explain: In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine puts 19...Bh3 first and the retreat Bc8 at least 1.5 pawns lower. Evidence at one depth, not proof.

feedback_by_move.d7c8: The retreat Bc8 is rated at least 150 centipawns below 19...Bh3 at depth 16.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is Bg2+.
Bxf2 is at least 80 centipawns below the top move.

hints: List Black's checks first; then ask which one leaves the white king the fewest options.
One check comes from a bishop that a white pawn could take; ask whether that pawn can.
The bishop gives check on g2, and after the king steps aside the same bishop can capture on f3 with check.
items.explain: In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine puts 20...Bg2+ first; the capture 20...Bxf2 is at least 80 centipawns lower. Evidence at one depth, not proof.

feedback_by_move.b6f2: Taking the pawn is rated lower: Bxf2 is at least 80 centipawns below 20...Bg2+ at depth 16.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine finds a forced mate starting with Rg2.
In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is Rg2 and the game move Bg2+ is also a forced mate.

hints: Black has a check that keeps the initiative. Is there also a quiet move that makes threats?
Look at the second rank: which white pawn and which square would a rook on that rank hit?
The rook on g6 goes to g2, next to the white king.
items.explain: In a four-line search at depth 16 the engine finds a forced mate after 22...Rg2, and also after the game move 22...Bg2+, which is a little slower. Both win, so more than one move can be correct. Engine lines are evidence at one depth, not proof.

feedback_by_move.f3g2: The game move. At depth 16 the engine also finds a forced mate after it, slightly slower than after 22...Rg2, so it is accepted.
